findings.title: Double-clicking "Water now" records two waterings
findings.steps: On the Beds page, double-click "Water now" on a bed (or retry after a slow response). The button has no :disabled binding, and the API has no protection against duplicates or idempotency key.
findings.actual: Two waterings with the same timestamp are recorded, and the dashboard and history show both.
findings.evidence: beds.vue: the Water now <button> has only @click="waterNow(bed)" and no :disabled, while the Save button does have one. Two POSTs of {"bed_id":1} in a row returned 201 twice, creating ids 3 and 4 with the same watered_at of 2026-11-12 11:41:30 (I deleted them afterwards).

findings.title: A huge bed_id or watering id gives a 500 instead of a 4xx
findings.expected: A 422 or 404 with a readable reason.
findings.actual: 500 Internal Server Error, because SQLite overflows on integers above 64 bits.
findings.evidence: All three requests returned 'Internal Server Error 500'. Opening /waterings?bed=99999999999999999999 in the app triggers the same 500 from the page.

findings.title: Waterings page and dashboard error states have no retry
findings.steps: Make GET /api/waterings fail (for example, the server is down), then open the dashboard or the Waterings page.
findings.expected: An error message with a Retry button that refetches without a reload.
findings.actual: Only an AlertMessage appears with no retry control. The dashboard does not even destructure refresh for waterings. On /waterings, a failed refetch after a filter change can show the error above a stale list of earlier results.
findings.evidence: index.vue: `const { data: waterings, error: wateringsError } = wateringsResult` has no refresh, and the template has no retry button. waterings.vue: the error alert has no button, and the table renders whenever waterings has data, even if wateringsError is set.

findings.title: If loading beds fails, the waterings bed filter is silently empty
findings.steps: Make GET /api/beds fail while GET /api/waterings succeeds, then open /waterings.
findings.expected: An error saying the bed list could not be loaded, with a retry.
findings.actual: The Bed select shows only "All beds" and no error appears, so the user cannot filter.
findings.evidence: waterings.vue: `const { data: beds } = bedsResult`. The error is ignored and the template uses `beds ?? []`.

findings.title: An invalid ?bed= query shows a raw validation message and a filter that doesn't match
findings.expected: The bad filter is ignored or explained in plain words.
findings.actual: The page shows the alert "Query.bed id: Input should be a valid integer, unable to parse string as an integer". The select matches no option, and the Clear filter button is the only way out.
findings.evidence: The SSR HTML of /waterings?bed=abc contains role=alert with that text.

findings.title: Absurd past dates are accepted (for example 0001-01-01)
findings.steps: Enter the date 0001-01-01 and 1 litre, or POST {"bed_id":1,"watered_on":"0001-01-01","litres":1}.
findings.expected: The date is refused with a reason, or a reasonable lower bound is enforced.
findings.actual: It is saved with 201 and appears in the history as year 1.
findings.evidence: The POST returned 201 with id 5 and watered_on 0001-01-01 (deleted afterwards). Only future dates are validated.

findings.title: Requests to the watering endpoints have no 10 s timeout
findings.steps: Make the API hang on POST /api/waterings, then click Save watering.
findings.expected: The request fails after 10 s with a visible error, and the button becomes usable again.
findings.actual: The button stays on 'Saving…' or 'Watering…' for as long as the request hangs.
findings.evidence: useApiClient / useApiFetch set no timeout option. The new pages use them without one.
